simple.meaning: שֹׁד (shôd) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “violence , ravage.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 25 times across Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and 5 more, beginning at Job 5:21. Its contexts include Torah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שֹׁד (H7701).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שֹׁד (shôd) / H7701 is traced through Job 5:21, Job 5:22, Psalms 12:6, Proverbs 21:7 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue,
You will laugh at destruction and famine,
Yahweh’s words are flawless words,
The violence of the wicked will drive them away,
for their hearts plot violence
Wail, for Yahweh’s day is at hand! It will come as destruction from the Almighty.

Let my outcasts dwell with you! As for Moab, be a hiding place for him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortionist is brought to nothing. Destruction ceases. The oppressors are consumed out of the land.
Therefore I said, “Look away from me. I will weep bitterly. Don’t labor to comfort me for the destruction of the daughter of my people.
These two things have happened to you—
Their feet run to evil,
Violence shall no more be heard in your land,
As a well produces its waters, so she produces her wickedness. Violence and destruction is heard in her. Sickness and wounds are continually before me.
For as often as I speak, I cry out;
The sound of a cry from Horonaim,
“ ‘The Lord Yahweh says: “Let it suffice you, princes of Israel: remove violence and plunder, and execute justice and righteousness; dispossessing my people,” says the Lord Yahweh.
Woe to them!
For, behold, they have gone away from destruction.
Therefore a battle roar will arise among your people,
Yahweh also has a controversy with Judah,
Alas for the day!
